definition_text: Zero trust (ZT) provides a collection of concepts and ideas designed to minimize uncertainty in enforcing accurate, least privilege per-request access decisions in information systems and services in the face of a network viewed as compromised.
source_document: NIST SP 800-207, Zero Trust Architecture (August 2020) — KB 2/USA/NIST.SP.800-207.pdf

definition_text: Zero trust architecture (ZTA) is an enterprise’s cybersecurity plan that utilizes zero trust concepts and encompasses component relationships, workflow planning, and access policies.
source_document: NIST SP 800-207, Zero Trust Architecture (August 2020) — KB 2/USA/NIST.SP.800-207.pdf

definition_text: Therefore, a zero trust enterprise is the network infrastructure (physical and virtual) and operational policies that are in place for an enterprise as a product of a zero trust architecture plan.
source_document: NIST SP 800-207, Zero Trust Architecture (August 2020) — KB 2/USA/NIST.SP.800-207.pdf

definition_text: The “implicit trust zone” represents an area where all the entities are trusted to at least the level of the last PDP/PEP gateway.
source_document: NIST SP 800-207, Zero Trust Architecture (August 2020) — KB 2/USA/NIST.SP.800-207.pdf

definition_text: The trust algorithm (TA) is the process used by the policy engine to ultimately grant or deny access to a resource.
source_document: NIST SP 800-207, Zero Trust Architecture (August 2020) — KB 2/USA/NIST.SP.800-207.pdf

definition_text: The control plane is used by various infrastructure components (both enterprise-owned and from service providers) to maintain and configure assets; judge, grant, or deny access to resources; and perform any necessary operations to set up communication paths between resources.
source_document: NIST SP 800-207, Zero Trust Architecture (August 2020) — KB 2/USA/NIST.SP.800-207.pdf

definition_text: The data plane is used for actual communication between software components.
source_document: NIST SP 800-207, Zero Trust Architecture (August 2020) — KB 2/USA/NIST.SP.800-207.pdf

definition_text: Security fatigue [3] is the phenomenon wherein end users are confronted with so many security policies and challenges that it begins to impact their productivity in a negative way.
source_document: NIST SP 800-207, Zero Trust Architecture (August 2020) — KB 2/USA/NIST.SP.800-207.pdf
